text:
sam: heads-up — we're seeing a cluster of fncall validation failures show up as billing spikes in eu-west-1, need to decide chargeback behavior
priya: yup, noticed that. failures are mostly schema_mismatch on streaming tool outputs, often mid-stream after a few tokens :grimacing:
alex: are these coming through the strict canary? which route id?
priya: route=summary_v2_canary, request ids look like req_abc123, req_def456. sample payload attached in console link: https://console/redwood/samples/req_abc123
jess: quick question: if we auto-fallback to degen variant, who gets billed — the original route or the fallback pool? currently metrics split is messy
mike: historically we billed whichever backend processed tokens. problem is the console attribution for customers — they see spikes on summary_v2 even though we moved to degen on validation error
sam: ops ask: for rejected fncall (schema mismatch) should we bill at all? policy A: charge full tokens up to reject. policy B: don't charge tokens if validation fails server-side. opinions?
priya: leaning B for customer trust, but that means we need to handle fraud/abuse surface where models spit gibberish and we get no revenue.
alex: compromise: soft-charge small flat fee for rejected calls, or mark as "validation_failure" in billing with reduced unit rate. then attribute to original route for invoicing clarity
jess: console UX: we should show a validation badge on the route page with counts, plus a toggle to enable auto-fallback-to-degen and show simulated cost impact before enabling
mike: telemetry needs: add validation_score (0-1), failure_reason, request_id, route_id, snapshot of first N tokens. Also mark whether fallback triggered and which model handled remainder
priya: example of error payload I'm parsing:
```
{
  "error": "schema_mismatch",
  "field": "items",
  "expected": "array",
  "got": "string",
  "request_id": "req_abc123",
  "route": "summary_v2_canary",
  "position": 42
}
```
this happens mid-stream and we have partial tool output persisted in KV cache
alex: KV cache persistence complicates retries/fallbacks — if we route to degen after partial KV writes we can serve inconsistent data to downstream calls
sam: operational constraints: we can't arbitrarily rewind KV without explicit snapshot/transaction. so fallback needs to be stateless or use new session id
jess: rollout plan thought: for canary set soft-validate=true so we surface failures but still let responses through; after 1 week, flip strict=true and enable auto-fallback with conservative billing rules
mike: need console telemetry panel: per-route "validation loss" heatmap, per-account rejected-token count, and a link to sampled payloads with quick-replay button. also spec for the billing tag: validation_status in metering events (ok, soft_fail, hard_reject)
priya: question for legal/compliance: storing sampled token snapshots — retention limits and PII scrub rules? cc @deploy-bot for policy deploys
deploy-bot: FYI: retention policy 90d for sampled payloads; PII-scrub pipeline will redact emails/SSNs before shown in console starting next deploy
alex: implementation note — we should emit a single unified event when a fncall crosses validation boundary: {event: "fncall.validation_outcome", route, req, validation_score, action_taken} (telemetry engineers can recommend final schema)
sam: final ask — can infra team spike a patch that: 1) tags metering events with validation_status, 2) adds fallback attribution field, 3) surfaces samples in console with scrubbed tokens? I'll open a follow-up ticket
priya: thanks — I'll draft the billing policy doc (options A/B/compromise) and propose defaults for canary vs prod. tagging follow-up as RFC-169
jess: i'll mock console wireframes for the badge and quick-replay button and share tomorrow :thumbsup:
mike: if anyone's prototyping, pls include tests for streaming fncall midstream-failure, KV consistency, and billing attribution
sam: cool, that's the plan. ping me on thread when RFC is ready. :raised_hands:
